chunks: And from him, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about fox skins: may one perform salat (prayer) in them? He said: "I do not like to perform salat (prayer) in them."
And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, who said:
I wrote to him asking him about salat (prayer) in rabbit skins, and he wrote: "It is disliked."
Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Bunan ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Abhari, who said:

I wrote to him: May I be your ransom, we have socks and waistbands made from rabbit fur. Is salat (prayer) permissible in rabbit fur without necessity and without taqiyyah? So he wrote, عليه السلام: "Salat (prayer) in them is not permissible."

Ibrahim ibn 'Uqbah wrote to him: We have socks and waistbands made from rabbit fur. Is salat (prayer) permissible in rabbit fur without necessity and without taqiyyah? So he wrote, عليه السلام: "Salat (prayer) in them is not permissible."

key_terms.تَقِيَّةٍ: dissimulation for protection under constraining circumstances
key_terms.جُلُودِ الثَّعَالِبِ: fox skins used as garments or material for clothing
key_terms.وَبَرِ الْأَرَانِبِ: rabbit fur or hair used in garments

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) valid in clothing made from fox skin or rabbit fur according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: These narrations address the ruling on performing salat (prayer) in garments made from fox skins and rabbit skins or fur. The reports indicate dislike regarding fox skins, and they state that salat (prayer) in rabbit fur garments is not permissible without necessity or taqiyyah.
